extracted.intended_audience: aspiring short-story writers and fiction authors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting short stories that feel complete and impactful, focusing on theme, plot, climax, human resonance, and originality. Advice is aimed at making each story tightly shaped and precisely worded rather than meeting arbitrary length targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Central idea must be clear and cohesive. 'Everything that happens in that story should be able to tie back to that idea.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every incident, image, and line of dialogue connects to the story's central idea so the narrative feels unified rather than a sequence of scenes. Treat theme as the organizing principle that gives meaning to events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning, middle, end with character development. Per Robert Barr: develop the plot 'letting no incident creep in that does not bear relation to the climax.' Plot must be simple, plausible, logical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear setup, development, and resolution; avoid extraneous incidents or subplots that don't serve the climax; keep the plot economical, believable, and logically consistent with characters' actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climax-Centered Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything leads to a single, powerful conclusion. Climax should feel both surprising and inevitable. Every word advances toward this moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shape the story so each scene, detail, and sentence increases pressure toward the climax; aim for a moment that resolves central tensions in a way that reads as both unexpected and earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Even fantastical stories must explore authentic human experiences. Readers connect through recognizable aspects of the human condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground actions and stakes in believable emotions, relationships, or dilemmas so readers empathize with characters, regardless of setting or genre; prioritize human truth over gimmick.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Short story readers demand freshness. Clichés and tropes less tolerable than in novels. Original execution essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tired plots, familiar tropes, and predictable language; strive for fresh perspectives, surprising details, or distinctive voice to hold reader interest in a short form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision Over Word Count (bonus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfect length is 'exactly how long it needs to be to be good.' Focus on eliminating unnecessary words rather than hitting word-count targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit for economy and precision: trim anything that doesn't serve the story's theme, plot, or climax rather than trying to meet an arbitrary length. The right length is whatever best delivers the story's effect.
